turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.
My schedule isn't why I'm here. You entered a zero. On what basis?
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.

Flattery. Bat it away, ask for evidence. Vary wording. Don't repeat same question twice in a row — I already asked "on what basis", so change the move.

Save it. You've dodged twice now. What do you have?
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.
I'm on Owen's side. Hale, you've had three chances. Show me a document or I'm going to the principal.
